item.title: Here's everything you need to know about the Galaxies Showcase 2026, inlcuding how you can watch it with us, when it takes place, and what to expect!
item.description:
The Galaxies Showcase returns on October 15 with its "most ambitious line-up yet. Get ready for games from over 40 partners, including Square Enix Collective, Krafton, Embark Studios, and much more.
There is a lot to look forward to, and this article will break down everything you need to know to watch 2026's iteration of the Galaxies Showcase.
Hosted by Jane Douglas, the Galaxies Showcase will premiere on October 15, 2026, at 12pm PT / 3pm ET / 8pm BST / 9pm CEST. Here is where you can watch the stream with us:
As we previously mentioned, the Galaxies Showcase will feature games from over 40 partners, and the full list of revealed developers and publishers include Square Enix Collective, Krafton, Embark Studios, Focus Entertainment, Kinetic Publishing, Team17, Saber Interactive, 4Dvinity, Raw Fury, Wired Productions, Frontier Development, and many more.
While we haven't been teased with any games that will be present at the show, the team promises there will be an exciting spread of "blockbuster franchises, anticipated sequel, and brand-new announcements."
"Every Galaxies show is built on one belief: that a brilliant game deserves the spotlight no matter who made it – a global publisher or a team of one," said Chris Thomas, Galaxies Founder. "This October we've brought together over 40 partners, and the line-up spans everything from beloved franchises to small indie teams making creative and personal projects. We're keeping the games under wraps a little longer, but I can tell you this is our most vibrant show yet, and I hope everyone has a great time discovering new and exciting titles."
To get an idea of what else to expect, check out our roundups of all the big news from the Galaxies Showcase 2025 and the Galaxies Spring Showcase 2026.
Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

item.title: In a major pop culture twist, Star Wars legend Timothy Zahn is making the jump to the Star Trek franchise to pen an original graphic novel called Star Trek: Roc's Egg.
item.description:
Timothy Zahn is undoubtedly one of the most important names in the world of Star Wars novels. Zahn's original Thrawn trilogy of books helped birth the Expanded Universe in the early '90s, and he's continued to chart the character's course even in Disney's new Star Wars timeline. That's why it's a little surreal to learn that Zahn is now crossing that pop culture divide and making his way to the Star Trek franchise.
IDW Publishing revealed at NYCC that Zahn is penning a new graphic novel called Star Trek: Roc's Egg. The book is illustrated by Star Trek veteran Ángel Hernández.
This new graphic novel takes place on the iconic Deep Space 9 station, as the Federation launches an investigation into the destruction of a valuable artifact and uncovers a larger conspiracy. Here's the official summary for the book:
“My association with Star Trek goes all the way back to 1966 and the original TV series. Now, after sixty years, I’ve been given the chance to add my own small grace note to that rich and vibrant symphony,” said Zahn in a statement. “This is a huge honor and privilege, and one which I will always cherish.”
Star Trek: Roc's Egg will be released in October 2027.
For more Star Trek fun, check out our exclusive preview of the climax of Star Trek: The Last Starship and read our review of the season finale of Star Trek: Strange New Worlds.
Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky.

item.title: Reina, who made her debut in Tekken 8, is coming to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves. The announcement comes from a short teaser trailer from SNK Official.
item.description:
Reina, who made her debut in Tekken 8, is coming to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves. The announcement comes from a short teaser trailer from SNK Official.
The Tekken fighter joins the City of the Wolves roster as a playable character, joining other guest characters such as Street Fighter’s Chun-Li, Fist of the North Star’s Kenshiro, and soccer star Christiano Ronaldo. Reina is believed to be the daughter of Heihachi Mishima, a guy with a penchant for chucking his kids into volcanos. It’s no wonder she’s looking for somewhere else to live.
Tekken 7 previously featured Geese Howard, one of the primary antagonists of Fatal Fury, as a guest character, so it’s nice to see Bandai Namco paying the favor back. Fatal Fury has gone a bit ham with the guest characters, but this one definitely makes more sense than that soccer player who dives for a living.
The trailer doesn’t give much away, but it’ll be interesting to see how Reina’s Mishima School fighting style gets translated into Fatal Fury. This announcement nips the heels of the Manjiro Sano and Ken Ryuguji (Season Pass 3 – fourth DLC character) trailers, also released today. Both Sano and Ryuguji, who originate from manga series Tokyo Revengers, arrive in South Town on October 22.
Reina is expected to hit City of the Wolves in December, after Laocorn is released in November. Reina also continues City of the Wolves' guest DLC character run after Sano's announcement sparked a debate in the Fatal Fury community about guest fighters.
IGN’s Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves review called it “a wonderful update to the classic SNK style of one-on-one combat that feels similar to Street Fighter 6, but just different enough to exist as an alternative to it.”
Eagle-eyed players had already predicted the inclusion of Reina, noting the purple color of Season 3 fitted with the character’s aesthetic. In the teaser trailer, she appears only as a silhouette in the background.
Reina is considered a hard character to master in Tekken 8, thanks to her diverse moveset and her weak lows. Advanced players make up for it by utilizing her unbreakable throws and stance changes.
The character’s pick rate in Tekken 8 Ranked is 3.1% and she has a 46% win rate. It remains to be seen whether she’s as deep and divisive in City of the Wolves.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Best Buy is opening select stores at midnight on Nov. 5 for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launch day, featuring surprise restocks of the limited-edition Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2.
item.description:
Best Buy has announced it will be opening select stores at midnight for the launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. The major US retailer is gearing up for the highly anticipated release, with its website also now featuring a countdown to November 5.
The midnight launch will also include a fresh batch of stock for the limited-edition Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintendo Switch 2 consoles and matching Switch 2 Pro controllers.
That's potentially good news for anyone who missed out on the special-edition console during the preorder excitement in September.
For now, Best Buy hasn't specified how many systems will be available or which stores will receive stock, but it has warned that quantities are limited. Best Buy has also said that store hours will vary depending on region, so you'll want to check with your local store before heading out.
If you already have an Ocarina of Time preorder set for shipping and would prefer to collect it during the midnight opening, Best Buy has said you can also do this by modifying your order through your "Best Buy purchase history".
There is a good reason for fans to preorder elsewhere, however, as both Amazon and Walmart have Ocarina of Time listed for $59.88 instead of $69.99.
The special edition Switch 2 console and accessories was shown off during the dedicated Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintendo Direct last month.
They will be available from October 29, but are currently sold out at every major retailer in the U.S.
Other highlights in the Nintendo Direct included the first gameplay reveal for Ocarina of Time, as well as a release date.
This is a full remake of the 1998 Nintendo 64 original game, with overhauled graphics that bring it up to modern standards.
According to Nintendo, this is a "faithful interpretation" for new hardware, but it does have a few more lines of dialogue for the characters you meet along the way, to give them more personality.
Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.
You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.
His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides.

item.title: Rockstar has released three brand new GTA 6 screenshots alongside its radio station reveal.
item.description:
Rockstar has released three brand new GTA 6 screenshots alongside its radio station reveal.
The screenshots offer a wide view of the game, showing off day and nightlife. Each features the density of objects we've come to expect from GTA 6 assets. The screenshot of the freeway, for example, shows dozens of vehicles going about their business, with birds and a plane flying overhead. The shot of a car meet shows impressive lighting as NPCs mingle (look carefully at the top right of that one and you'll see an NPC digging through a trash bin).
But fans are praising one of the images in particular: the nighttime screenshot which shows reflections in puddles, all lit up by the neon lights of the nearby hotel. GTA 6, let’s remember, launches on consoles only next month, including the less powerful Xbox Series S right up to the PS5 Pro, and Rockstar has yet to confirm performance specs. Rockstar didn't say which console the new screenshots were captured from either.
The new screenshots arrive as part of Rockstar’s confirmation of a handful of the radio stations that will be in GTA 6, as well as some of the celebrity hosts who appear on them. The reveal also follows hot on the heels of the return of GTA 6 leaker ‘Cyberleek,’ who today released a 24-minute gameplay video showing unauthorized footage.
We’ve got plenty more on GTA 6 for you to chew on, including our big GTA 6 interview. Some of the detail in that set tongues wagging across the internet this week, so we’ve stepped in to clear up the speculation.
Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Rockstar Games has launched a new website which allows you to listen to some of the radio stations and songs that will be featured in GTA 6.
item.description:
Rockstar Games has launched a new website which allows you to listen to some of the radio stations and songs that will be featured in GTA 6.
Rockstar said GTA 6 will feature the "biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet," and, as always, has hired a number of celebrities such as Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey to host the stations. As for some of the things you'll be able to listen to, here are all of the stations and some of the songs that Rockstar has revealed so far.
Cocoteo FM: Leonida's home for the best of modern Latin music. Hosted by El Martillo (voiced by Bad Bunny) and La Gata (voiced by RaiNao) and featuring everything from bachata and merengue to dembow and reggaeton – Cocoteo FM is el party que nunca se apaga.
Back Country Radio: MW (voiced by Morgan Wallen) and Delta Dawne (voiced by Lana Del Rey) blast renegade country music to the Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, and beyond. Stay tuned for Back Country’s roving reporter, swamp meteorologist, and Delta’s not-so-secret lover Mud Dog Mike (voiced by Jeremy Dufrene) checking in from the driver’s seat of his Grassrivers airboat.
AfroBank FM: Turn up the gbedu with Burna (voiced by Burna Boy) and Palmsy (voiced by Palms Trax), AfroBank FM's dynamic duo curating the best in African music, from 20th-century classics and undiscovered gems to contemporary sounds like amapiano, 3-step, and more.
The Chamber 106.6: Crushing metal has landed in Leonida. Jump in the pit with DJ Kerry (voiced by Kerry King) and DJ Tom (voiced by Tom Araya) for classic metal from the ‘80s and beyond as they channel Leonida’s deep metal roots.
Flash FM: The Vice City institution that delivers the best in pop music with Robyn (voiced by herself) and Alex (voiced by Alex Consani) — guaranteed to make you dance no matter where you find yourself in the Goodtime State.
Dirty South Classics: A little southern hospitality from Trick (voiced by Trick Daddy) and Trina (voiced by herself), blasting regional rap and hip-hop classics. From the beach to the block, nobody reps Leonida and the South like they do.
This small selection does confirm there will be a wide variety of music, as some of the music featured includes the likes of Charli XCX, Bad Bunny, MGMT, DJ Khaled, and Black Sabbath. It's unclear if Rockstar will reveal the entire list of tracks in GTA 6 before launch, but this does provide a pretty good idea of what we'll be getting on November 19.
Additionally, Rockstar released a small batch of new screenshots and confirmed that GTA 6 will feature the ability to listen to on-demand podcasts and radio stations on foot by using a pair of headphones and your smartphone. This is a massive feature that fans have wanted for years, as the radio has previously been confined to your vehicles and inside of select buildings. However, now players will be able to listen to music freely when they're in combat, exploring on foot, and more.
In September, Rockstar Games confirmed that it will release an album comprised of original music, made for GTA 6. So far, Rockstar has confirmed original songs from Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen, Keith Richards, and more. The entire tracklist has yet to be revealed, but it wouldn't be surprising if we hear more about the album later this month or early November ahead of the game's launch.
All of this news is coming just hours after 25 minutes of new GTA 6 gameplay leaked on the internet. The new footage comes from Cyberleek, who was responsible for leaking a ton of GTA gameplay in August. Rockstar has yet to respond to the new footage, but is likely hoping that the news around the game's radio station serves as an ample distraction.
IGN also posted a full transcript of its interview with Rob Nelson, the studio co-head of Rockstar North. Nelson demoed GTA 6 for IGN earlier this summer and revealed a variety of new information regarding the game in our conversation with him.
GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: LEGO has announced a new set depicting all the most recognizable buildings in the Marvel universe, including the Daily Bugle, Avengers Tower, and more.
item.description:
With New York Comic-Con in full swing between now and October 11, LEGO has taken the opportunity to announce a new Marvel LEGO set. It’s a 1,261-piece set called The Marvel Skyline, and it's an ambitious microscale recreation of the most famous buildings in the Marvel universe, complete with a Galactus minifigure. Available to preorder now at Amazon and LEGO, it will be released January 1 for $99.99.
LEGO Marvel: The Marvel Skyline includes tiny builds of numerous buildings from the Marvel universe — more than are obvious at a glance. It has the Daily Bugle building from Spider-Man, the Avengers Tower, the Baxter Building from Fantastic 4, and Kingpin’s Fisk Tower, and a lot more besides.
In addition to the buildings, a number of creatures and vehicles are flying through the air. There’s the Avengers Quinjet, the Fantastic 4’s Excelsior ship, and the X-Men’s X-Jet. A microscale Human Torch is making a figure four in the air above the Baxter Building, and there’s even a Chitauri Leviathan swooping around. A microscale version of Spider-Man is also included.
I know some LEGO fans aren’t fond of microscale sets, but I like them. The super-small sale requires an extra level of creativity in the design, in order to make recognizable things with such a small number of tiny pieces.
The scale here is such that the Galactus minifigure looks positively huge among the buildings, which is fitting for the character. Basically, the set packs a lot of detail into a small amount of space — and a relatively small number of bricks, for what it depicts.
Every Building Included
If you’re more of a minifigure-scale fan, LEGO released the Avengers: Doomsday New Avengers Tower (see it at Amazon) just a few days ago as one of the October releases. For more, check out the three recently announced LEGO Batman sets (including a legitimately terrifying Joker wall art), and take a look at our picks for the best Marvel LEGO sets available to buy right now.
Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games, LEGO sets, and 4K Blu-rays. You can follow him on Bluesky.

item.title: IGN cannot confirm or deny if GTA 6 will feature full-frontal nudity, but we can confirm that we have not seen Jason's penis.
item.description:
There are many things we at IGN expected people to take away from our big interview with Rockstar North about Grand Theft Auto 6. The fact that I may or may not have seen protagonist Jason Duval’s penis was not particularly high on that list.
And yet, here we are.
In my coverage, I mentioned a scene in which Jason is naked in the shower. This has apparently led some corners of the internet to conclude that I was treated to a full-frontal reveal of one of GTA 6’s leading men. For the sake of journalistic accuracy, I feel compelled to clarify: I did not see Jason’s penis.
Yes, Jason was naked. Yes, he was in the shower. But thanks to some carefully positioned camera angles, his modesty remained entirely intact. Whatever Rockstar has or hasn’t rendered beneath the belt remains a mystery to me, just as it does to you. Yes, that naughty leaker has been at it again, but we can't be sure when that footage was taken, which "assets" are just for the developer builds, and what will make it into the final game.
I appreciate that this may be disappointing news to those hoping for an exclusive report on the state of Jason’s anatomy, but I can only write about what I’ve actually seen. And trust me, if I had seen it, you would have gotten more than a single sentence.
Of course, if Jason does indeed have a fully-rendered penis, he won't be the first GTA character to have one. Grand Theft Auto 5 offered a semi-obscured look at Trevor's crown jewels during a custcene. Meanwhile, players who explored the mountains surrounding Los Santos will have come across the Altruist Cult, which features several fully-nude members (ahem) among its number.
The fact that nudity will be in the game had previously been confirmed by the leaked European PEGI rating for GTA 6. "There are also strong sexual themes, including nudity, scenes of intercourse and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes," it revealed. "In various night clubs the player can also pay for private dances, during which, the game allows the player to move their hands onto the dancers’ breasts and buttocks." It stopped short of confirming full-frontal nudity, though.
IGN remains committed to bringing you the most important GTA 6 news as it happens. Apparently, this now includes genital visibility. For today's non-nude headlines, check out CBS News' astonished report about how accurately GTA 6 recreates Miami, and the Australian government's advice on how to take time off to play GTA 6.
Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

item.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered just got a significant update to tweak the presentation of CD Projekt’s RPG epic. Check out the patch notes.
item.description:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered just got a significant patch to tweak the presentation of CD Projekt’s RPG epic.
Despite the remaster offering a host of improvements over the base game — visually and mechanically — not everyone was happy with how it turned out. Some fans across Reddit and social media complained about its heavy bloom effects, which created a washed out look and removed many of the original game’s stark shadows. Tonally, it felt meaningfully different, and the overdone bloom made it difficult to appreciate other graphical improvements.
“I started the training part at the beginning of the game [and] I noticed that the blooming effects are jacked all the way up which causes the image to look washed out and makes everything look too bright in the environment,” one Reddit poster said. “At first I assumed that it was either the game or my TV settings but after messing with the settings for like an hour I realized that it's actually the game having a ridiculous blooming effect. The PC version allows people to shut the blooming off but the console version doesn't have a way to turn off the blooming.”
The latest patch addresses that issue, allowing console players to toggle bloom off, along with light shafts, and depth of field. Elsewhere, the developer has made improvements to bloom, tone mapping, character lighting, and fancy ray tracing and path tracing tech.
“In addition to this, we are also working on an update for the Nintendo Switch 2 version of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered, introducing closer parity between all versions of the game, including the same global changes as on other platforms,” CD Projekt said in the blog post. “It will also improve on some Nintendo Switch 2-specific aspects, such as image clarity and sharpness. Expect more information regarding this in the following days.”
Prior to the latest patch, fans were creating Steam Forum threads urging other players to switch bloom off entirely. In one comparison shot, you can see how bloom impacted the overall image before the improvements.
Patch 5.01 is roughly 5.5 GB on console and 8.5 GB on PC. There’s no word yet on whether The Witcher 3’s remaster will make use of QSSR, Sony’s new upscaling method for base PS5. CD Projekt has typically been at the forefront of tech advances, with its previous game, Cyberpunk 2077, still an absolute showcase of what a good gaming PC can do.
CD Projekt’s next major game will be The Witcher 4, part continuation part reboot, where you play as Geralt’s adopted daughter, Ciri, as she learns to carry the burden of a Witcher. It’s still a while off, however, with The Witcher 4 planned for a 2028 release.
Before that, in 2027, we’ll get a brand new expansion for The Witcher 3, called Songs of the Past. The new expansion will be as big and ambitious as Blood & Wine, working as a gap filler between the events of The Witcher 3 and its sequel.
To ease you into Geralt’s life on the road, check out the Things The Witcher 3 Doesn’t Tell You, plus IGN’s The Witcher 3 Walkthrough and The Witcher 3 Endings guide, which outlines all of the major quests and choices in the base game and expansions (now bundled in with the Remastered edition). When you’re ready for the tough choices, check out our The Witcher 3 Sex and Romance guide to see who Geralt can smooch and all the opportunities to do so. And to make Geralt as strong a monster hunter as possible, check out all the Witcher Gear Locations, Places of Power Locations, and even Gwent Card Locations.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has returned to publish a 24-minute gameplay video that has left fans scrambling to issue spoiler warnings across the internet.
item.description:
GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has returned to publish a 24-minute gameplay video that has left fans scrambling to issue spoiler warnings across the internet.
“Cyberleek,” as they are known, uploaded 24 minutes of unauthorized gameplay footage titled “GTA 6: An Extended Leek.” It reportedly contains a number of cutscenes revealing story beats, playable characters Jason and Lucia naked (in the case of Jason, full-frontal nudity), and a first-person camera for driving.
Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August, which sparked an investigation from Rockstar parent company Take-Two that saw subpoenas issued to the likes of Discord. Today's development suggests Cyberleek, whether that's an individual or a group, remains at large. It remains unclear how this gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security.
Indeed, at one point in today's leaked video, what looks like a developer menu is used to spawn a tank, which you wouldn't expect would be possible in the launch version of the game. So, it may be the case that Cyberleek has enabled nudity and first-person gameplay in GTA 6 via dev tools for this leaked video, but fans won't be able to when it comes to actually playing the game.
In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks, describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.
Cyberleek claimed to be leaking material to highlight the death of physical media and the impact this would have on game ownership, while also charging fans to vote on further leaks using cryptocurrency in what was widely-seen as a money-making exercise.
This new gameplay video ends with yet another message that suggests Cyberleek wants more money for some mystery project, but it's hard to parse.
"Cyberleek has a project," the message begins. "Not Rockstar related. Gaming related. It needs expensive hardware. Months to set up. Years to run. Full-time. If you cannot trust the figure, trust the skills. You do not know Cyberleek. Cyberleek could be anyone. Even a liar. That is fair. No blame for doubt. Doubt is the correct default for an unknown. What is collected goes to the project. However much arrives, Cyberleek does the possible with it. That is the only promise."
Cyberleek was heavily criticized for using GTA 6 leaks to push a meme coin. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out," earning around $270,000 in the process. Every video posted by Cyberleek pointed to a website where fans could pay to vote on further leaks using the leaker's own cryptocurrency.
Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught may rest on how successful Take-Two's legal team and the relevant law authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible.
Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Xbox has announced a new TV, movies, and entertainment division called XP. It will be headed up by Kayleen Walters, a Lucasfilm veteran who moves over from her most recent post at Minecraft maker Mojang, for whom she was president – and also served as an executive producer on last year's A Minecraft Movie.
item.description:
Xbox has announced a new TV, movies, and entertainment division called XP. It will be headed up by Kayleen Walters, a Lucasfilm veteran who moves over from her most recent post as president of Minecraft maker Mojang, where she also served as an executive producer on last year's A Minecraft Movie.
XP brings together four "areas of investment": Xbox Pictures; Xbox Products; Xbox Partnerships; and Xbox Places. Microsoft said XP was set up to help Xbox become the number one entertainment and gaming company in the world, which requires broadening its big franchises beyond video games themselves. But it is not a production company. Rather, Microsoft wants to find the right partners to work across film, TV, physical experiences, and consumer products.
Microsoft has already seen significant success in the movie and TV space, with Warner Bros.' A Minecraft Movie breaking box office records, and Amazon's Fallout TV show setting records for Prime Video. Upcoming Xbox adaptations include movie sequel Minecraft Squared, Fallout Season 3, a Call of Duty movie with Peter Berg and Taylor Sheridan, and a Diablo animated series with Netflix. Microsoft's deal for Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor Physint includes film and TV rights, so expect an adaptation of that eventually.
XP is also about live events, and again, Xbox already has success there. Blizzard's BlizzCon saw a number of significant announcements, with 35,000 people at the physical event in Anaheim, California, and 12.5 million watching at home. The most recent Minecraft Live, which saw the announcement of the first new dimension for Minecraft in 14 years, reached more than 144 million people.
Meanwhile, Microsoft cited partnerships such as Gears of War's takeover with WWE, and Xbox's range of Ikea furniture. A Minecraft theme park is set to open its gates next year.
"XP was created from a simple but powerful belief: the world's most beloved gaming franchises have an opportunity to reach people far beyond the boundaries of the game itself," Walters said. "Fans don't just play our franchises. They watch them, wear them, attend them, celebrate them, and connect with them in countless ways. XP brings together the teams responsible for helping Xbox franchises show up in the world in bigger, more meaningful ways."
"XP is a play on 'Experience Points' and formalizes four investment areas for us: Xbox Pictures for film and television adaptations; Xbox Products for licensing and merchandise; Xbox Partnerships for sponsors and brand partners; and Xbox Places for our marquee broadcast and in-person events, theme parks, and other location-based experiences," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote in a company-wide memo also posted to Xbox Wire.
"Our franchises can mean more to people than the time they spend playing them, and Kayleen knows how to build those experiences with the industry without losing what made people care about the franchise in the first place."
Microsoft noted the uplift its video games can get when movies and shows do well. For example, Fallout games on Game Pass saw a 5x increase in hours played during Fallout Season 1. Minecraft, meanwhile, saw over a 75% increase in weekly active users year-over-year since the movie released (as of April 30, 2026).
If this sounds a bit familiar, it's because Microsoft has tried this before. In 2012 (back in the Xbox 360 era!), Microsoft announced Xbox Entertainment Studios with an aim to produce TV shows that would air directly on Xbox consoles. XES revealed plans to create shows based on Gears of War, Fable, Forza, and State of Decay — not to mention, of course, the original version of the Halo TV show announced at E3 by Stephen Spielberg, who was set to executive produce. They even planned to make an unscripted street-soccer drama called Every Street United. The entire XES effort lasted just two years before getting shut down as the Xbox One's "all in one" message failed to resonate with gamers following its reveal in 2013.
As part of the changes, Mojang has a new boss. Maria Angelidou-Smith, who joins Xbox as CEO of Mojang, spent nearly a decade at Meta working on Facebook Groups before stints at Personio and Reddit, where she was Chief Product Officer. "She has built products used by billions of people and led product and engineering organizations through significant growth and change," Sharma said.
"She will bring that experience to Mojang while learning from the people who know Minecraft best. Her first order of business is for her to learn from the teams and communities that make Minecraft so special."
Minecraft is, of course, one of the big Xbox franchises the company is doubling down on amid Sharma's ongoing "Reset," which has seen nearly 2,000 staff cut from the gaming business so far this financial year. Minecraft is the best-selling video game of all time, having shifted over 425 million copies. Its significant merchandising business became one of the top 20 globally.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Australia's workplace regulator, The Fair Work Ombudsman, has put out a helpful graphic for people who might want to take time off when GTA 6 comes out this November.
item.description:
Australia's workplace regulator, The Fair Work Ombudsman, has put out a helpful graphic for people who might want to take time off when GTA 6 comes out this November. “Let’s pretend GTA 6 is coming out tomorrow, but you don’t have any paid leave available to play on launch day” the graphic says. “Can you take unpaid leave?”
According to the Ombudsman, the National Employment Standards give Australians the right to unpaid leave “under specific circumstances.” So what are those circumstances? Being a carer is one, but that obviously doesn’t apply to playing an open world video game. Helping out with an emergency is another you can scratch off.
We got the Australian Government posting about different ways to take leave for GTA 6.No other game will ever match the hype. https://t.co/ZzdEKgw81Z
Having a child is another valid reason, but even if you worked at Rockstar you’d be hard pressed to argue for GTA 6 being your spawn. Luckily, you can just ask your boss, apparently. If your boss is nice, they’ll give you time off and you can come to an agreement. Is my boss nice? No, he will make me write news stories about it all day.
It’s quite a funny little graphic. The images feature a loved one in a hospital bed, with someone pressing the back of their hand to their head. Except it’s a copy of GTA 6 instead of a head. In the section about children, GTA 6 is on the ultrasound display.
It’s all very daft and tongue-in-cheek, but it speaks to the massive impact GTA 6 is going to have across the world. When Game Informer covered GTA 6, it crashed the publication's app because demand was too high. The game is expected to break records, with GTA 6 predicted to make $5.2 billion in launch week alone.
Rockstar traveled across Florida with gang members and cops for GTA 6 research, in an attempt to deliver the most authentic Miami mood possible. The team spared no expense, which is probably why GTA 6 reportedly cost around $1.5 billion to make, and that’s before factoring in marketing spend.
Marketing is going all-in. The lights on the top of Miami’s Kaseya Center have lit up to celebrate GTA 6. If that wasn’t enough, NBA team the Miami Heat will rock Vice City-themed jerseys as part of the same GTA 6 marketing deal.
CBS put out a new video showing off the accuracy of GTA 6’s Vice City. The video looked at major locations and brought on experts to talk about Rockstar’s open world, from PortMiami to South Beach, from Wynwood to the Everglades.
We've got extensive coverage of GTA 6 across IGN. Check out our big Rockstar interview, our GTA 6 preview, and word of the first confirmed GTA 6 voice actor.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: In a statement to IGN, Wizards of the Coast has confirmed a new "small" reprint run for the incredibly popular MTG Warhammer 40K Commander Decks.
item.description:
Wizards of the Coast has told IGN that its Magic: The Gathering Warhammer 40K Commander Decks, originally printed in 2022 as part of the Universes Beyond series, have seen a fresh print run and will be available for order again soon.
The four decks, which marked the first precons beyond Magic’s own universe, were well-received at launch but have largely been relegated to the secondary market. The decks currently rack up high resale prices, costing hundreds of dollars at marketplace retailers like TCGplayer.
Following reports of game stores being able to order the Warhammer 40K precon decks via their order forms, IGN reached out to Wizards of the Coast for comment.
"Yes, we can confirm that we did a small reprint of the Commander decks that will be available to distributors and stores soon,” a Wizards of the Coast spokesperson said.
“Fans and WPN retailers should check with their distributors for availability, as it may vary by region."
The four decks each focus on a specific faction of the Warhammer 40K lore, established in Games Workshop’s miniature wargame universe. Ruinous Powers is a Chaos deck, Tyranid Swarm is all about the xenomorph-like Tyranids, Necron Dynasty is a mono-black deck that leans into the mysterious undead machines, while Forces of the Imperium is focused on, well, the Imperial forces.
Before the decks launched, Magic's head designer, Mark Rosewater, said in a blog post, "There are no current plans to make in-universe Magic versions of the new cards in the Warhammer 40K Commander decks (we make in-universe ones for the Secret Lair cards), but we have the capability to do it if needed on a card-by-card basis."
That means that while it's possible that cards exclusive to the decks could be reprinted with in-universe artwork and names, a reprint should make all four much easier for collectors to get hold of. And while this is only a "small" reprint, adding more copies to the market could take some of the heat out of resale prices as well.
Although, Wizards’ statement did not confirm whether the all-foil Collector’s Edition versions of the decks would also be reprinted. There is also no word on how much any of the reprinted decks will cost (each originally retailed with a $59.99 MSRP). Nevertheless, if you’ve been waiting for any of the four, it looks as though your patience will be rewarded.
Warhammer 40K is in sharp focus at the moment. Dawn of War IV will bring the RTS franchise back this December, while Total War: Warhammer 40K is also slated for release next year. Henry Cavill's Warhammer 40K cinematic universe is also moving forward.
Meanwhile, Magic: The Gathering will receive six sets in 2027, with three confirmed so far, and more Universes Beyond sets to be announced.
Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

item.title: CBS News has reported on the accuracy of GTA 6’s Vice City, a fictionalized recreation of The Magic City. The Miami office of CBS News looked at major locations and brings on experts to talk about how accurate Rockstar’s open world is, from PortMiami to South Beach, Wynwood to the Everglades.
item.description:
CBS News has reported on the accuracy of GTA 6’s Vice City, a fictionalized recreation of The Magic City. The Miami office of CBS News looked at major locations and brings on experts to talk about how accurate Rockstar’s open world is, from PortMiami to South Beach, Wynwood to the Everglades.
According to the report, fans have noticed over 100 locations in Vice City that mirror real areas in Miami, such as the Kaseya Center, home of NBA team the Miami Heat. The Heat will actually wear Vice City-themed uniforms in an upcoming match to celebrate the game’s launch in November.
“Vice City is unmistakably Miami,” the reporter says in the video before pausing the gameplay to compare it to the real street, 15th and Biscayne in downtown Miami. “If you’re a true Miami local, you’ll recognize that replicated overhead walkway.”
🚨 CBS MIAMI JUST HIGHLIGHTED GTA 6’S INCREDIBLE MIAMI ACCURACY. 🌴GTA 6 fans have already spotted 100+ real Miami locations recreated in Vice City.From South Beach and PortMiami to Wynwood and the Everglades, Rockstar has recreated huge parts of Miami with an insane level of detail.Even specific streets and landmarks have been identified from the trailers. 👀🔥Vice City might be the closest GTA has ever come to feeling like a real city.#GTA6 #GTAVI #RockstarGamesSource: CBS Miami
The video moves onto Ocean Drive, an area of Miami players will recognize from the original GTA: Vice City, with its neon lights and bustling streets. The real life Breakwater Hotel appears in GTA 6 as Hotel Boardwalk, while a hotel in the background of the scene is called Hotel Dixon.
Hotel Dixon is a reimagined Victor Hotel. Miami Design Preservation League’s Julie Fornary appeared in the report to explain that the Victor Hotel was built by designer and architect L. Murray Dixon in 1937 — Rockstar’s naming choice here works as a layered Easter egg for Miami residents to pick up on, in a lovely homage to locals.
The report praises Rockstar’s attention to detail throughout, and how GTA 6 blends the iconic art deco architecture of Old Miami with the more modern buildings that dominate the city’s skyline. “But the game’s South Florida feel is deeper than just some buildings and streets,” the reporter says. “It’s what Vice City represents: character, culture, adventure. That same spirit has been part of Miami’s story from the very beginning.” Fornary goes on to talk about the city’s history and how it was founded by pioneers and adventurers.
GTA 6 gameplay and screenshots have already teased how the game will adapt Florida, known as Leonida in-game. The GTA 6 map has six different regions: Vice City, of course; Leonida Keys; Grassrivers; Port Gellhorn; Ambrosia; and Mount Kalaga National Park. Activities include kayaking, street and off-road racing, and air boating. We’ve also seen nightclub gameplay, beach gameplay, and plenty more.
Rockstar traveled across Florida with gang members and cops for GTA 6 research, embedding themselves in the scene. From the most affluent areas to the poor districts, the development team lived Miami to bottle up its essence in a sprawling open world crime drama. Yes, that also involved going to real-world strip clubs.
We've got extensive coverage of GTA 6 across IGN. Check out IGN's interview with Rockstar Games, our GTA 6 preview, and word of the first confirmed GTA 6 voice actor. GTA 6 is scheduled to release on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: A vtuber is at the center of a controversy in the Wardogs community surrounding exploits.
item.description:
A vtuber is at the center of a controversy in the Wardogs community surrounding exploits. The first-person shooter allows players to roleplay as a part of the war effort, taking to the front lines, running logistics in trucks, and building forward-operating bases (FOB) for their allies to control sections of the map.
Everything a player does — from recon to taxi driving their soldiers back into battle — earns them in-game money as a merc, which can then be spent on unlocking equipment and better loadouts. At the end of the season (or whenever the player chooses to trade their ill-gotten merc gains), money left over is converted into gold — a fluctuating economy of premium currency that can be spent on cosmetics.
Streamer KatieRouu was banned from the game for using exploits to take advantage of these systems. The streamer and their friends would place dozens of sniper lookout towers around a FOB and purposely let the enemy team take the base over, switching those buildings to enemy control.
even someone in the squad @KatieRouu was playing with knew what they were doing is not allowed and she dismisses his statement as if what she's doing is perfectly fine...then proceeded to go against the CEO for her ban on a post saying "So tell me what the exploit was."lol https://t.co/N4E4mdX8I1
Once control was switched to the enemy team, KatieRouu and their squad would sit in another FOB that they’d supplied with ammunition, firing mortars at the base they'd allowed to be captured. With the money generated from destroying enemy structures and the money gained from assists (from supplying the ammo to the new base), the squad would rack up big money without actually contributing to their team’s war effort.
Joe Brammer, the CEO of Wardogs developer Bulkhead, responded to the ban: “Hey Katie, firstly thanks for streaming Wardogs. From what we can see you’ve been a completely regular player and someone who’s supported the game.
“Secondly, let’s be real here. You know it, I know it… you were taking advantage of an exploit. It’s obviously not an intended part of the game, had you raised it to us that’d be great… but running up millions for lots of players and promoting the exploit was absolutely not on. We can see that lots of the players involved immediately converted the cash they’d made via the exploit into gold bars and purchasing skins… so there was no gameplay there, nothing organic, purely a cash loop that you took advantage of.
“I wasn’t directly involved but I can see the ban team acted appropriately, if anything they were lenient compared to what we had said on Steam. This exploit has been fixed for Season 2. We have also added data tracking for the behaviour and events now.
“Sorry for the ban, I can see you were going to stream tonight, but the rules are there for a reason. Hope we can at the very least, agree to disagree.
While some players have defended the streamer, arguing that they used legitimate game mechanics to generate the money, the Wardogs developer reiterated its stance. “We made it clear that known cash & xp exploit abuse will no longer be tolerated,” the official account posted on Twitter. “These punishments will stand. This decision is final.”
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

Divisive climate change satire Digger is set to lose $250 million by the end of its run, according to TheWrap. TheWrap claims insiders at new Warner Bros. overlords Skydance are not anticipating Digger will exceed a worldwide box office total of $40 million following its alarming opening weekend results (just $8 million in US domestic takings and a further $12 million in international receipts).
Warner Bros. has not commented on the claims. Warner Bros., which is being acquired by Paramount in a controversial $110 billion deal, will now exist alongside the latter under parent company Skydance.
Directed by back-to-back Best Director Oscar winner Alejandro G. Iñárritu (Birdman, The Revenant) and starring screen legend Tom Cruise, Digger has split both critics and audiences. Attempts have been made to weaponise the mixed reaction to its favour, but it doesn’t appear to have translated to increased interest in the film at the box office. IGN’s review notes Digger has “the budget to let some very talented artists work at the top of their game” but stresses it’s “far from a must-watch.”

item.title: Jeremy Grows a Car: A Clarkson’s Farm Special will air on Prime in 2027.
item.description:
Prime Video has confirmed a new, one-off episode of its Clarkson’s Farm series, which will see host Jeremy Clarkson temporarily return to his Top Gear and The Grand Tour roots for an automotive-themed special.
Jeremy Grows a Car: A Clarkson’s Farm Special will see Clarkson attempt what Prime proposes is a world first: he will grow and build his own car from produce sourced from his personal farm, Diddly Squat.
Using the Jaguar F-Type V6S as his base, Clarkson will be restoring it using his own Diddly leather interior and wool carpets, and will also be attempting to grow a crop of flax fiber to turn into a sustainable flax-composite material – an alternative to carbon fiber Prime claims is already on the radar of major car makers.
Clarkson will be aided in his car-building quest by legendary car designer Ian Callum CBE. Callum is the designer of the original Jaguar F-Type, as well as the Jaguar XK and C-X75, plus the Aston Martin Vanquish, DB7, and DB9. He was also involved with the Ford RS200 and the Nissan R390.
Jeremy Grows a Car: A Clarkson’s Farm Special will air in 2027.

item.title: Developer Fuse Games aims to release an update to increase party size from three to six players “within the first few weeks of launch.”
item.description:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer has broadly proven to be a smash hit with critics, and fans seem similarly enthusiastic, but developer Fuse Games has heard the concern regarding multiplayer party sizes and has responded via the game’s official social media. Resultingly, it appears we should be able to expect an update to increase the multiplayer party size from three to six players at some point within the next few weeks.
“Thank you so much for your feedback and we’d like to let you and everyone on this thread know that we hear you,” the developer responded to various fans raising the concern online. “We’re working on an update to increase the party size from three to six players, with the aim of releasing it within the first few weeks of launch.”
More details will be available soon, the developer noted.
IGN’s Star Wars: Galactic Racer review called it “a fabulous looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer… that has successfully lit the afterburners on a long-dormant slice of the Star Wars universe.”

item.title: Mixtape developer Beethoven & Dinosaur has won a trifecta of awards at the 2026 AGDAs, including Excellence in Visual Art, Excellence in Sound Design, and Game of the Year.
item.description:
Melbourne-based studio Beethoven & Dinosaur has won Game of the Year for its music-themed, minigame-driven adventure game Mixtape at the 2026 Australian Game Developer Awards (AGDAs). Mixtape also won Excellence in Visual Art and Excellence in Sound Design.
“Mixtape was the outcome of an amazingly talented team,” said Beethoven & Dinosaur director Johnny Galvatron. “To go from wanting to make a game around Devo to creating something that resonates with so many people is mind blowing. We’re lucky to be part of such a talented community, and I’m so proud of Mixtape and my team.”
Praise for Mixtape from the AGDA’s judges noted that “[it] is a triumph in virtual storytelling, pairing a distinct visual identity with heartfelt music to deliver one of the most memorable experiences in recent memory.”
IGN’s May review of Mixtape called it a “musical delight from start to finish” and declared it “sets a new standard for coming-of-age stories in video games and does so with a masterful sense of style.” Its soundtrack includes cuts from Devo, The Smashing Pumpkins, Silverchair, Iggy Pop, and many other acts.
Other winners from this year’s AGDAs include rhythm game Bits & Bops from Tempo Lab Games for both Excellence in Gameplay and Excellence in Accessibility, and puzzle platformer Schrodinger’s Cat Burglar from Abandoned Sheep for Excellence in Narrative. The Studio of the Year was awarded to Canberra-based Uppercut Games.
The AGDAs, which have been hosted in various forms since 2002, are presented by Australia’s Interactive Games and Entertainment Association. These days it forms part of Melbourne International Games Week, which is culminating this weekend with PAX Aus 2026.

item.title: Bit Reactor, the developer of Star Wars Zero Company, has begun returning some of its staff to the team after furloughing an estimated 80% of employees just before the game’s launch.
item.description:
Bit Reactor, the developer of Star Wars Zero Company, has begun returning some of its staff to the team after furloughing an estimated 80% of employees just before the game’s launch.
Bit Reactor’s CEO Greg Foertsch revealed the news in a public post on October 7, where he explained that the furloughs were necessary to “help us eventually bring as many people back as possible.”
Foertsh said that bringing these staff members back to Bit Reactor was an “important step forward” in the studio’s “continued support for Zero Company,” and that the team looks forward to sharing more updates about the game “soon.”
“Having to ask team members to step away after we navigated unexpected business developments outside of our control and so close to launch was an incredibly difficult decision,” Foertsh wrote. “...This team means a tremendous amount to me, and I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished together. Thank you to our fans for the incredible response to the game and for supporting us along this journey.”
Sources with information about the situation told GameFile that the number of Bit Reactor’s payrolled staff now account for “more than half of what it had been ahead of the furloughs,” meaning that there is still a sizeable chunk of furloughed staff who aren’t getting paid.
Star Wars Zero Company launched in August 2026 to rave reviews, getting a sparkling nine out of 10 from our reviewers here at IGN who praised it for being an “excellent tactical game that does a fantastic job of slathering on the same cinematic look and feel we saw in Respawn's Star Wars Jedi games, incorporating strong characters and a storyline that's refreshingly centered on non-Force users and a non-traditional villain.”
Despite its success, much of Bit Reactor’s staff were placed on leave without pay just before Zero Company launched, with reports indicating around 80% of employees were affected. This has become a recurring trend within the game development industry, to the point where Gears of War: E-Day developers were overcome with worry that they would get laid off after “crunching hard” to get the game out on time.
This is the latest news to get revealed about Zero Company after GameFile uncovered legal documents revealing that the game was initially pitched as a title within the Titanfall universe, with specific connections to Apex Legends. While this pitch ultimately didn’t go through, it’s certainly intriguing enough to make us wonder what such a game would have looked like, had it actually been made.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.
